newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn mostly lower on good growing weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn mostly lower on good growing weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were showing modest losses early Thursday, pressured by nearly ideal crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Some forecasters were calling for widely scattered showers in the western Midwest with high temperatures ranging from 73 to 84 degrees Fahrenheit.

However, the nearby July contract was underpinned slightly by USDA net old crop export sales of 516,800 tonnes. That figure came in above trade expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes. New crop corn sales were at 256,200 tonnes, below expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
In early trade, Cargill Investor Services sold one million bushels December, ABN Amro Chicago Corp sold 500,000 bushels July and Continental Grain bought 500,000 July, pit sources said.
At 1007 CDT, July corn was down 3/4 at $2.65-3/4, and other months were down 1-1/2 to 1/4 per bushel.
